summary: Game crashes when player model is rendered after the player is stung by a bee
description: The bug When getting stung by a bee, the game crashes as soon as the player model is rendered. To reproduce There are multiple ways to reproduce this issue: Inventory - Get stung by a bee - Open your inventory Third-person camera - Enable third-person camera - Get stung by a bee Crash report 19w39a : [^crash-2019-09-27_13.19.08-client.txt] Description: Rendering entity in world java.lang.IllegalStateException: Not filled all elements of the vertex at cxk.a(SourceFile:253) at dwx.a(SourceFile:56) at dyd.a(SourceFile:48) at dyd.a(SourceFile:14) at duw.a(SourceFile:138) at dym.a(SourceFile:64) at dym.a(SourceFile:41) at dtz.a(SourceFile:268) at dtz.a(SourceFile:253) at dgt.a(SourceFile:134) at dgt.a(SourceFile:106) at dfx.render(SourceFile:82) at dgm.render(SourceFile:42) at dgt.render(SourceFile:86) at dpo.a(SourceFile:603) at dat.d(SourceFile:931) at dat.b(SourceFile:569) at net.minecraft.client.main.Main.main(SourceFile:199)
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.
2. Create a new Creative world with default settings.
3. Enable third-person camera mode.
4. Get stung by a bee.
5. Wait until the player model is rendered.
6. Observe that the game crashes immediately after the player model is rendered.
Observed Behavior: When a player gets stung by a bee, the game experiences a crash immediately upon rendering the player model. This issue can be reproduced through various methods, such as getting stung by a bee while the inventory is open or while using the third-person camera view. The crash report generated during this event indicates an IllegalStateException, specifically stating that not all elements of the vertex have been filled. The error message references several source files, including cxk.a, dwx.a, and dgt.a, which suggests a problem in the rendering process of entities within the game world. This bug has been observed in the version 19w39a, and the crash report can be found under the filename crash-2019-09-27_13.19.08-client.txt. The behavior disrupts gameplay by causing the application to close unexpectedly, making it critical for developers to address this rendering issue related to player models after being stung by bees.
Expected Behavior: When a player gets stung by a bee, the game should continue to function normally without crashing. The player model should be rendered correctly, allowing the player to interact with the inventory or switch to third-person camera mode without any issues. This expected behavior ensures a smooth gaming experience, where players can enjoy the consequences of bee stings without encountering unexpected crashes or errors in the rendering process.
